content.title: Recap: Timberwolves, Hawks complete dramatic comebacks
content.text: Hawks steal one at MSG, Timberwolves even series in Denver and more from Monday's slate. What a night! Relive the best of Monday night’s action in the 2026 NBA Playoffs with the NBA.com live blog. Donovan Mitchell (30 pts, 7 reb, 5 ast) starred as the Cavaliers took Game 2 over the Raptors 115-105 to open the night, earning a 2-0 series lead. The Hawks rallied in the final moments behind CJ McCollum (32 pts), winning the fourth quarter 28-15 to defeat the Knicks 107-106 on the road and even the series at 1-1. The Timberwolves won a back-and-forth battle in Denver, coming back from 19 down to defeat the rival Nuggets 119-114 and tie their series 1-1. All-Access: Raptors-Cavaliers All-Access: Hawks-Knicks All-Access: Timberwolves-Nuggets Sunday’s live blog: Celtics, Thunder, Magic and Spurs start 1-0 2026 NBA Playoffs hub Download the NBA App What we know after Monday’s games: The Cavaliers are up 2-0 on the Raptors, while the Hawks-Knicks and Timberwolves-Nuggets series are tied 1-1. Check out the postgame pressers. Hawks-Knicks Raptors-Cavaliers Timberwolves-Nuggets We’ll reconvene these series Thursday with a Game 3 triple-header on Prime. Knicks vs. Hawks, 7 ET Cavaliers vs. Raptors, 8 ET Nuggets vs. Timberwolves, 9:30 ET APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:46 ET Monday’s results Cavaliers 115, Raptors 105 Hawks 107, Knicks 106 Timberwolves 119, Nuggets 114 Nikola Jokić (24 pts, 15 reb, 8 ast) is your top performer of the night, followed closely by James Harden (28 pts, 5 reb, 4 ast, 5 stl). APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:41 ET Postgame Presser: Timberwolves-Nuggets APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:25 ET ‘Minnesota! A shocker, here in Denver’ The Timberwolves fought back to defeat the Nuggets 119-114 in a battle between familiar Western Conference foes, coming back from 19 down to prompt the capping call from Michael Grady. Jamal Murray (30 pts) had a chance to cut the lead to one with 11 seconds to go, but his shot was long. Donte DiVincenzo (16 pts) grabbed the board, prompting a give-and-go fast break that he capped with a game-sealing slam. “It’s 1-1. There’s no driver’s seat,” said Anthony Edwards (30 pts, 10 reb, 3 3PM). “Hopefully, our fans rattle them a little bit when they come to our crib. We’ll be ready.” The Nuggets and Timberwolves have played 30 times since 2022-23. They played with the focus built by familiarity tonight, trading huge plays down the stretch. Nikola Jokić (24 pts, 15 reb, 8 ast) was brilliant in defeat. APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:20 ET Back-and-forth we go These teams are trading ridiculous plays. Gobert dunked on Jokić. Donte DiVincenzo hit a cold-blooded 3-pointer. Joker slashed to the rim for a poster on Gobert. High quality basketball in full flight. 115-113 Minnesota with 30.6 seconds to go, Nuggets ball. It’s the 2026 NBA Playoffs, folks. APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:13 ET Timberwolves rally into the lead 110-107 Minnesota with 3:36 to go. Delivering some trademark hustle and spark, Donte DiVincenzo (11 pts) assisted Jaden McDaniels with a transition dime, then scored a fast break layup of his own to send Minnesota to a timeout. APRIL 21, 2026 / 1:06 ET Nuggets holding slim lead 107-104 with 5:54 to go in the fourth quarter. Anthony Edwards (30 pts) and Julius Randle (20 pts, 5 ast) put up the last four Timberwolves points, while Christian Braun (14 pts) prompted a Minnesota timeout with a big driving jam. These two Northwest Division rivals are going toe-to-toe in one of the best games of the 2026 NBA Playoffs so far. Tune in to NBC and Peacock and end your night with some quality hoops! APRIL 21, 2026 / 12:53 ET ‘This game is insane’ Brian Scalabrine aptly noted in the middle of a run that included back-to-back 3-pointers by Bruce Brown (7 pts) and eight straight points from Naz Reid, including a thunderous one-hand slam. 101-98 Denver with 9:40 to go in the fourth. APRIL 21, 2026 / 12:47 ET The Joker leads Denver to a three-point lead Nikola Jokić (22 pts, 12 reb, 7 ast) scored 14 points in the third quarter, helping Denver to a 93-90 lead. Anthony Edwards (28 pts) is delivering enough for a duel, though. Catch the finish on NBC and Peacock! APRIL 21, 2026 / 12:41 ET Takeaways: Raptors-Cavaliers, Game 2 NBA.com’s Shaun Powell shares his observations after the Cavaliers took Game 2, defending home court before heading up north. “Given the stakes and the situation, this served as the high-water mark for the Mitchell-Harden backcourt tandem which was formed at the trade deadline a few months ago. They were fluid and forceful and a handful Monday for the Raptors and really through both games. This was precisely what the Cavaliers hoped for when they fused these two stars together and now they’re reaping the benefits of that decision. Both players are capable of going downhill and attacking the rim for layups or fouls, or shooting from 15 feet and beyond. It’s a combination that’s tough to defend, even for a decent group of Toronto defenders… There was a stretch where Mitchell had 17 points in 20 minutes and Harden 19 in 19, an impactful 1-2 punch.” APRIL 21, 2026 / 12:33 ET ‘We’ve got a heavyweight fight’ Austin Rivers said as Nikola Jokić (18 pts, 11 reb, 7 ast) finished a tough finish in the post through Jaden McDaniels, drawing and converting the and-one to give the Nuggets an 85-79 lead with 4:13 to go in the third. These teams have played more than anyone in the NBA since 2022-23. It feels like it tonight — both are giving no quarter. The Timberwolves will look to find something from Rudy Gobert down the stretch. The veteran center has not yet scored and is a team-low -10. APRIL 21, 2026 / 12:23 ET Going back-and-forth in Denver 75-73 Minnesota with 6:21 to go in the third quarter, as Anthony Edwards (22 pts, 7 ast, 7 reb) heads to the free throw line for a potential three-point play. APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:57 ET Tied at 64 at the half in Denver What a half! The Nuggets led by as many as 19 before the Timberwolves rallied back, taking an eight point lead of their own with two minutes to go. Denver then closed on an 8-0 run, capped by a 51-foot Jamal Murray (23 pts) buzzer-beater from well behind half court. “When we have a lead, cherish it,” said Tim Hardaway Jr. (14 pts). Anthony Edwards (20 pts) and Julius Randle (18 pts) powered the offense for Minnesota. APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:54 ET Wolves in the lead 64-58 with 1:11 to go in the second quarter, as the Timberwolves have scored on 10 straight possessions. APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:44 ET Wolves keep running 49-48 Timberwolves with 5:27 to go in the second quarter, as Anthony Edwards (17 pts) manages to hang in the air and convert the layup to retake the lead in the Mile High City. Minnesota’s on a 24-4 run to get back in the contest. APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:39 ET One time for CJ McCollum APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:33 ET Wolves on a run 11-0 run for Minnesota to cut the Denver lead to 44-36 with 8:20 to go in the second quarter. Anthony Edwards (14 pts) and Julius Randle (12 pts) are the top scorers for the Timberwolves, with Edwards dropping seven in this quarter. APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:15 ET Postgame Pressers: Hawks-Knicks APRIL 20, 2026 / 11:03 ET Wolves look for spark against Nuggets Denver’s used a 13-0 run to take a 20-11 lead with 5:04 to go in the first quarter on NBC and Peacock, holding Minnesota to 28% shooting so far. Anthony Edwards (3 pts), who was questionable with right knee inflammation, is limping some after colliding with Nikola Jokić (3 reb, 4 ast) in the back court, but staying in the game. Search for inspiration, Chris Finch just put in Bones Hyland, looking for some creativity off the bounce. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:46 ET Hawks defeat Knicks to even series 1-1 In a dramatic finish, Mikal Bridges’ game-winning jumper was just short, as the Hawks stormed back in the fourth quarter to defeat the Knicks. CJ McCollum (32 pts) inspired the Hawks with his play, drawing the ire of the Madison Square Garden crowd in the win. “I’m just here to compete, and here to compete at the highest level,” said McCollum afterwards. “We’re a tough group. We’re young, but we’re learning by the day.” Jalen Brunson (29 pts) led six Knicks in double figures. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:44 ET Big shot Brunson Jalen Brunson’s 3-point rolled around every part of the rim, but fell through to cut the Hawks’ lead to 107-106. Atlanta ball with 7.1 seconds remaining. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:41 ET A frenetic Hawks comeback It’s 107-103 Atlanta, stunning the New York crowd. CJ McCollum has seven points for Atlanta in the last two minutes, while the Knicks have only mustered a single Jalen Brunson 3-pointer in the last 5:16. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:33 ET Hawks get it to one 100-99 New York with 3:26 to go in the fourth quarter. The Hawks have controlled the period 20-9 to get it to this point. Catch the finish on NBC and Peacock! APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:28 ET Knicks holding off Hawks The Hawks had it to four, but the Knicks scored two straight buckets to make it 100-92 with 5:25 to go in the fourth quarter. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:17 ET KAT in the Big Apple Towns is up to 18 points and 8 rebounds, facing a smaller Hawks front line. This is where they miss Kristaps Porziņģis. APRIL 20, 2026 / 10:04 ET Emotions high in New York 89-77 New York with 2:03 to go in the third quarter after former Pelicans teammates Jose Alvarado and CJ McCollum drew offsetting technicals, continuing what has been a feisty game. “(Hawks) need some fight, need some life,” said Jamal Crawford. “This is where vets matter.” Alvarado picked up McCollum on the next possession, dogging him full-court as the crowd roared its approval. McCollum waved to Ben Stiller and Spike Lee, sitting front row in the Garden, afterwards. APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:58 ET Postgame Pressers: Raptors-Cavaliers APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:47 ET Knicks take biggest lead of game 77-64 over Atlanta, with six New York players in double figures. The Knicks are up to a dominant 43-19 advantage on the glass, putting up 55 shots to Atlanta’s 47. APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:35 ET Cavaliers hold off Raptors’ challenge to take Game 2 Cleveland defeats Toronto 115-105, winning Game 2. “The Cavaliers have been the best version of themselves in Games 1 and 2,” said Mark Followill. “Now, the series moves north.” James Harden (28 pts, 5 reb, 4 ast, 5 stl), Donovan Mitchell (30 pts, 7 reb, 5 ast) and Evan Mobley (25 pts, 8 reb on 11-of-13 shooting) starred in front of the Rocket Arena crowd. It was the fourth time in the Cavs’ Playoff history that they’ve had three players drop 25+ points. “Continue to be mentally strong,” said Mitchell of the Cavaliers’ future plans. Scottie Barnes (26 pts) and RJ Barrett (22 pts) led the way for the Raptors in defeat. APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:30 ET Knicks lead 61-54 at the half After Atlanta came back to take its first lead, New York reasserted control to end the second quarter in the lead as they seek to defend Madison Square Garden. Jalen Brunson (12 pts, 6 ast) leads four Knicks in double figures, while CJ McCollum (18 pts) has a game-high for Atlanta. APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:20 ET Starting Lineups: Timberwolves-Nuggets, Game 2 Nikola Jokić and the Nuggets host Rudy Gobert and the Timberwolves as their 2026 NBA Playoffs series continues on NBC and Peacock. Stats listed from Saturday’s Game 1, which the Nuggets won 116-105. Game 2 (9:30 ET) is coming to you on NBC and Peacock. Minnesota: PG Donte DiVincenzo (12 pts, 4 3PM) SG Anthony Edwards (22 pts, 9 reb, 7 ast) SF Jaden McDaniels (16 pts, 8 reb) PF Julius Randle (16 pts, 7 reb) C Rudy Gobert (17 pts, 10 reb) Denver: PG Jamal Murray (30 pts, 7 ast) SG Christian Braun (12 pts, 8 reb) SF Cameron Johnson (12 pts, 2 3PM) PF Aaron Gordon (17 pts, 8 reb) C Nikola Jokić (25 pts, 13 reb, 11 ast) Keep an eye on Naz Reid off the Timberwolves’ bench in Game 2. He had 5 points in Game 1 — well below his season average of 13.6 ppg. It was the second-lowest scoring total of his career against Denver. APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:11 ET Barrett on the boards RJ Barrett (18 pts, 9 reb) just tied his season-high in rebounds as the Raptors shrink the lead to 92-86 with 6:46 to go in the fourth quarter. Barrett’s single career-high for rebounds is 15, which he’s done twice. Catch the finish on NBC Sports Network and Peacock! APRIL 20, 2026 / 9:00 ET Raptors, Hawks cut into leads The Raptors have it to seven after three quarters in Cleveland, with the Cavs up 84-77, while the Hawks have slashed the Knicks lead to 40-36. APRIL 20, 2026 / 8:45 ET Knicks up 32-23 after one New York held Atlanta to 37.5% shooting, knocking down 54.5% of their shots, and totaled a remarkable 20-4 advantage in the first quarter. Josh Hart (6 pts, 6 reb) and Mitchell Robinson (6 pts, 4 reb in 4:32) have been the main culprits so far, crashing the boards as Quin Snyder tried Jalen Johnson as center, with Jonathan Kuminga as the power forward. APRIL 20, 2026 / 8:35 ET Brandon Ingram getting loose Back-to-back buckets for the Raptors’ top scorer (4 pts), who has finally broken the seal here in the third quarter. Ingram’s 2-of-9 in the contest so far, facing the size and length of Dean Wade and the Cavs’ front line. Cavs are up 68-55 with 7:37 left in the third quarter. APRIL 20, 2026 / 8:32 ET The Hart of the Knicks Josh Hart (6 pts, 4 reb, 2 ast) is off to a quick start for the Knickerbockers, who are up 20-13 with 4:09 to go in the first quarter. Hart put up a double-double with 11 pts and 14 reb in Game 1. We’ll see if the Hawks can match his activity and strength in crashing the glass here in Game 2. APRIL 20, 2026 / 8:13 ET Cavaliers up 54-48 at the half The Cavs have led wire-to-wire in the first half, with James Harden (16 pts) and Donovan Mitchell (15 pts) going off. The Raptors have a 24-5 advantage in bench points and a 9-0 lead in fast break points, but they’ve turned the ball over 11 times to the Cavaliers’ seven. RJ Barrett (10 pts, 6 reb) is the top man for Toronto so far. APRIL 20, 2026 / 7:58 ET Harden shakes loose James Harden just made Scottie Barnes touch Earth and got a ridiculous bounce on his stepback 3-pointer, putting the Cavaliers up 50-40 with 3:20 to go in the second. Harden has 16 pts on 6-of-8 shooting, including two 3-pointers made. APRIL 20, 2026 / 7:49 ET Starting Lineups: Hawks-Knicks, Game 2 Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks host the Atlanta Hawks in Game 2 of their 2026 NBA Playoffs series on NBC and Peacock. Stats listed from Saturday’s Game 1, which the Knicks won 113-102. Game 2 (8 ET) is on NBC and Peacock. Atlanta: PG CJ McCollum (26 pts, 4 3PM) SG Nickeil Alexander-Walker (17 pts, 4 ast) SF Dyson Daniels (9 reb, 11 ast) PF Jalen Johnson (26 pts, 7 reb) C Onyeka Okongwu (19 pts, 8 reb) New York: PG Jalen Brunson (28 pts, 7 ast) SG Mikal Bridges (11 pts, 1 stl) SF OG Anunoby (18 pts, 8 reb) PF Josh Hart (11 pts, 14 reb, 5 ast) C Karl-Anthony Towns (25 pts, 8 ast) Watch for Jonathan Kuminga off the Hawks’ bench — he had eight points on 3-of-7 shooting in Game 1, with the size to challenge the Knick wings. APRIL 20, 2026 / 7:37 ET Cavs up 26-19 after one Donovan Mitchell (7 pts) leads all scorers so far. For his career, he’s averaging 28.4 ppg in the NBA Playoffs, raising it by putting up 29.6 ppg in both 2023-24 and 2024-25. APRIL 20, 2026 / 7:27 ET Cavaliers’ vets exerting influence The Cavs are big enough to bother the Raptors at basically every position — one of the main advantages of the James Harden-for-Darius Garland swap — and experienced in the Playoffs. Harden, Mitchell and Allen are still the only Cavaliers to score, as Cleveland methodically works its way to a 19-12 lead with 4:02 to go in the first quarter. Neither Brandon Ingram nor Scottie Barnes has scored so far for Toronto. APRIL 20, 2026 / 7:17 ET Cavs hot early 12-7 Cavaliers with 8:14 to go in the first quarter, as Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Jarrett Allen have put in four points apiece, going 6-for-8 from the field. The Raptors had the fifth-best defensive rating in the NBA (112.1) during the regular season, but don’t have a ton of quick defenders to track Mitchell. RJ Barrett’s drawn the early assignment here. APRIL 20, 2026 / 6:30 ET Starting Lineups: Cavaliers-Raptors, Game 2 Brandon Ingram and the Toronto Raptors are looking to even their 2026 NBA Playoffs series against the Cavaliers on Peacock. Stats listed from Saturday’s Game 1, which the Cavaliers won 126-113. Game 2 (7 ET) is on NBC Sports Network and Peacock. Toronto: PG Jamal Shead (17 pts, 5 3PM) SG Brandon Ingram (17 pts, 56 FG%) SF RJ Barrett (24 pts, 3 3PM) PF Scottie Barnes (21 pts, 7 ast) C Jakob Poetl (6 reb, 2 blk) Cleveland: PG James Harden (22 pts, 10 ast) SG Donovan Mitchell (32 pts, 4 3PM) SF Dean Wade (5 pts, game-high +20) PF Evan Mobley (17 pts, 7 reb) C Jarrett Allen (10 pts, 7 reb) Watch out for Max Strus off the Cavaliers bench. The sharpshooter had 24 pts in 24 minutes in Game 1, including four 3-pointers and an 8-of-10 mark from the free throw line. APRIL 20, 2026 / 6:15 ET Tonight’s injury report Immanuel Quickley and Thomas Bryant are out for the Cavaliers. Jock Landale is out for the Hawks. Onyeka Okongwu is available. OG Anunoby is probable for the Knicks. Anthony Edwards is questionable for the Timberwolves. Peyton Watson is out for the Nuggets.
